results.title: Non-soluble products of non-conjugate maximal subgroups (Kourovka 10.34, Monakhov)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two maximal subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$. Here $MN$ is the set of products $mn$ with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$.

results.title: Finite groups that are the product of every two non-conjugate maximal subgroups are soluble
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two maximal subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$; here $MN$ is the set of products $mn$ with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.34 in the negative.

results.title: The norm commutes with base change
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $A'$ and $B$ be commutative rings, where $A'$ and $B$ are $A$-algebras and $B$ is a free $A$-module of finite rank. Then for every $b \in B$, the image of the norm $N_{B/A}(b)$ under the structure map $A \to A'$ equals the norm $N_{(A' \otimes_A B)/A'}(1 \otimes b)$ of $1 \otimes b$ in the $A'$-algebra $A' \otimes_A B$.

results.title: The trace commutes with base change
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $A'$ and $B$ be commutative rings, where $A'$ and $B$ are $A$-algebras and $B$ is a free $A$-module of finite rank. Then for every $b \in B$, the image of the trace $T_{B/A}(b)$ under the structure map $A \to A'$ equals the trace $T_{(A' \otimes_A B)/A'}(1 \otimes b)$ of $1 \otimes b$ in the $A'$-algebra $A' \otimes_A B$.

results.title: Norm in a product algebra is the product of norms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The norm of a product algebra is the product of the norms of the components: left multiplication by `(x₁, x₂)` is the product map of the left multiplications, and the determinant of a product map is the product of the determinants.

results.title: Norm on a subsingleton algebra is one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The norm on a subsingleton algebra is `1`: left multiplication by any element is the identity map on a subsingleton module, hence has determinant `1`.

results.title: Landau–Ramanujan theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real $x$, let $B(x)$ be the number of natural numbers $m \le x$, including $m = 0$, that can be written as $m = a^2 + b^2$ with natural numbers $a$ and $b$. results.title: Lattice points of a sector

results.summary: For a real number $\alpha$, let $S(\alpha) = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 0 \le y \le \alpha x\}$ be the sector of slope $\alpha$. Its lattice points are $I(\alpha) = S(\alpha) \cap \mathbb{Z}^2$, viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: The origin is a lattice point of every sector

results.title: Quadratic packing polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real function $P(x, y)$ of two real variables is a quadratic packing polynomial (QPP) on a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ if it is a polynomial of total degree two, that is, $P(x, y) = a x^2 + b x y + c y^2 + d x + e y + f$ for some real $a, b, c, d, e, f$ with $a, b, c$ not all zero, and $P$ maps $S$ bijectively onto the set $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ of natural numbers.

results.title: First occurrence of a value in a Gijswijt sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the first occurrence of $n$ in the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$ is the least position $k \ge 1$ with $A^{(m)}(k) = n$, and it is $0$ if $n$ does not occur in $A^{(m)}$.

results.title: Block lengths of the higher-order Gijswijt sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $A^{(m)}(k)$ for the $k$th term of the $m$th order sequence. The block lengths $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ are defined by $\beta^{(m)}(0) = 0$, $\beta^{(m)}(1) = 1$ and, for $t \ge 1$, $\beta^{(m)}(t+1)$ is the least $k > (m+1)\,\beta^{(m)}(t)$ with $A^{(m)}(k+1) = m$, or $0$ if there is no such $k$.

results.title: Gijswijt blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the block $B_t^{(m)}$ is the prefix of length $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$, where $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ is the $t$th block length.

results.title: Glue strings of a Gijswijt sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the glue string $S^{(m)}_t$ is the block $B^{(m)}_{t+1}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence with its first $(m+1)\,\beta^{(m)}(t)$ elements removed, where $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ is the length of the block $B^{(m)}_t$.

results.title: Concatenated glue strings of a Gijswijt sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, the string $T^{(m)}_t$ is the concatenation $S^{(m)}_1 S^{(m)}_2 \cdots S^{(m)}_{t-1}$ of the glue strings of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence; it is empty when $t \le 1$.

results.title: Block index of the first occurrence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, let $p$ be the position of the first occurrence of $n$ in the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence $A^{(m)}$, with $p = 0$ if $n$ does not occur. Then $t(m, n)$ is the least $t \ge 1$ such that the block length $\beta^{(m)}(t)$ equals $p$, so that when $n$ occurs, this first $n$ is the last element of the block $B_t^{(m)}$; if there is no such $t$, then $t(m, n) = 0$.

results.title: Block words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $u$ and exponents $a_1, a_2, \ldots$, the block word of order $m$ is the concatenation $B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_2^{a_2} B_1^{a_1}$, where $B_i = B_i^{(m)}$ is the $i$th block of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence and $B_i^{a_i}$ is $a_i$ copies of $B_i$ in a row. Only $a_1, \ldots, a_{u-1}$ are used, and the word is empty when $u \le 1$.

results.title: The first block has length one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, the first block length $\beta^{(m)}(1)$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence equals $1$.

results.title: The first block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $m \ge 1$, the first block $B_1^{(m)}$ of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence is the one-term string $m$.

results.title: The first concatenated glue string is empty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, the concatenated glue string $T^{(m)}_1$ is the empty string.

results.title: The empty block word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$ and every sequence of exponents $a_1, a_2, \ldots$, the block word $B_{u-1}^{a_{u-1}} \cdots B_1^{a_1}$ of order $m$ with $u = 1$, where $B_i$ is the $i$th block of the $m$th order Gijswijt sequence, is a product of no blocks and hence the empty string.

results.title: Retract
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $Y$ be a subgraph of a graph $X$. A *retraction* from $X$ to $Y$ is a homomorphism $f$ from $X$ to $Y$, regarded as a graph in its own right, whose restriction to the vertex set of $Y$ is the identity map. We say that $Y$ is a *retract* of $X$ if there is a retraction from $X$ to $Y$.

results.title: Core of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite graph $X$ is a *core* if every homomorphism from $X$ to itself is a bijection. For finite graphs $X$ and $Y$, $Y$ is a *core of* $X$ if $Y$ is a core, there is a homomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, and there is an injective homomorphism from $Y$ to $X$; that is, $Y$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $X$.

results.title: Local injection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A homomorphism $f$ from a finite graph $X$ to a finite graph $Y$ is a *local injection* if any two distinct vertices of $X$ with the same image under $f$ are at distance at least $3$ in $X$.

results.title: Local isomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A homomorphism $f$ from a finite graph $X$ to a finite graph $Y$ is a *local isomorphism* if for every vertex $x$ of $X$, $f$ maps the set of neighbours of $x$ bijectively onto the set of neighbours of $f(x)$.

results.title: Graph cover
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite graph $X$ *covers* a finite graph $Y$ if there is a surjective local isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$.

results.title: Folding of a graph homomorphism
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A homomorphism from X to Y is a *simple folding* if it has one fibre consisting of two vertices at distance two, and all other fibres are singletons. A homomorphism is a *folding* if it is the composition of a non-negative number of simple foldings.

results.title: Cost of a gap run
